[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] DartPoints own site describes a strategy of delivering enterprise grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure services to communities outside the largest United States metros, operating in Tier 2 and Tier 3 regional markets. The company began operations in the early 2000s. DartPoints is headquartered at 1601 Elm Street, Suite 3650, Dallas, Texas. This session refreshed and sharpened a prior research passes brief note that the company received a strategic growth investment from NOVA Infrastructure in 2025: per both DartPoints own press release and independent trade press corroboration from Data Center Dynamics, both fetched fresh this session, NOVA Infrastructure actually acquired majority control of DartPoints, announced April 30, 2025, with lending partner Orion Infrastructure Capital, committing more than 250 million dollars in combined growth capital, while the prior owner, Astra Capital Management, retained a meaningful minority stake. As part of that same transaction, DartPoints acquired the underlying real estate for three of its data centers, in Greenville, South Carolina, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and Asheville, North Carolina, per both sources. DartPoints own site lists 11 facilities across 10 markets, including Baton Rouge, Louisiana (2 facilities) and Shreveport, Louisiana, Cincinnati and Dublin, Ohio, Columbus, Indiana, Asheville, North Carolina, and Columbia, Greenville, Charleston, and Spartanburg, South Carolina, matching every state where this registry lists a DartPoints facility, and DCD independently corroborates the same 11 facility, 10 market count and adds that the company serves more than 900 enterprise customers including Fortune 500 companies, universities, and hospital systems. The company emphasizes AI ready, high density infrastructure, 99.999 percent uptime, and SOC 2 Type II compliance. This specific row, the Cincinnati, Ohio facility (internal code CVG01), per the operators own dedicated location page for this facility, fetched fresh this session, sits at 302 W 3rd St UNIT 400, Cincinnati, OH 45202.

reading.body:
DartPoints Cincinnati publishes 1.6 MW of IT capacity at a downtown Cincinnati address. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this represents roughly 40 racks, or if fully deployed for accelerator hosting at 10 kW per accelerator, roughly 160 units. The facility ranks eighth among eight Ohio data centers with published capacity figures, representing 2.6 percent of the state's published 60.4 MW.

DartPoints Cincinnati qualifies under SOC 2 Type II compliance for enterprise-grade colocation, cloud, and managed infrastructure. The operator emphasizes AI-ready, high-density infrastructure and 99.999 percent uptime across its portfolio. DartPoints is now majority-controlled by NOVA Infrastructure as of April 2025, with combined committed growth capital exceeding 250 million dollars across the operator's expansion.

This campus sits in Ohio, which has 76 mapped data center facilities but only eight with published power figures. Cincinnati's 1.6 MW is too small to move the needle on state-level AI scaling or grid constraints. Its relevance is to regional enterprise customers in a Tier 2 market, not to the national AI infrastructure build.
